stations.challenge: Choose three things that make a good life. Explain each choice to your partner.
followUpQuestions: Is success about money or happiness? Why?
What are you proud of?
Can success be different for two people? How?
stations.mainQuestion: What does success mean to you?
stations.stretch: Your partner says: “Money is the most important thing.” Do you agree? Explain why or why not.
stations.subtitle: What is important in life?
stations.title: What Is Success?

stations.challenge: Compare two students: one has top grades but no free time; the other has average grades and lots of friends. Who is happier?
followUpQuestions: What do grades show?
How do you feel before a test?
What helps you learn well?
stations.mainQuestion: How important are grades for your future?
stations.stretch: Invent a new way to say “well done” at school without giving a grade. Explain how it works.
stations.subtitle: Are good grades everything?
stations.title: Grades, Grades, Grades

stations.challenge: Your family wants one job for you; you want another. Role-play a polite conversation.
followUpQuestions: What advice does your family give you?
Is this advice always useful? Why or why not?
How can you explain a different choice?
stations.mainQuestion: Who should choose your future: you or your family? Why?
stations.stretch: Role-play the conversation again, but this time find a solution that is good for both of you.
stations.subtitle: What does my family want? What do I want?
stations.title: My Dream or Your Dream?

stations.challenge: Tell your partner two things they do well. Then ask: “How did you learn that?”
followUpQuestions: Does social media help or hurt? Why?
When can comparison be useful?
What makes you feel confident?
stations.mainQuestion: Why do people compare themselves with friends?
stations.stretch: Give two tips for feeling good when other people seem better than you. Explain them.
stations.subtitle: Are other people always better?
stations.title: Me and Other People

stations.challenge: Tell a short story: first a mistake, then a second try. What happened in the end?
followUpQuestions: Why are mistakes useful?
How can a friend help you after a failure?
What can you say to a friend after a failure?
stations.mainQuestion: What do you do when something goes wrong?
stations.stretch: A friend doesn’t want to try again after a mistake. Give her three tips and explain them.
stations.subtitle: What can we do after a mistake?
stations.title: Mistakes Are OK

stations.challenge: Plan one day with study, friends and rest. Compare plans.
followUpQuestions: What makes you tired?
How do you relax?
What can students change in their week?
stations.mainQuestion: How much free time do students have? Is it enough?
stations.stretch: A friend is always tired because he does too much. What can he stop doing? Give reasons.
stations.subtitle: School, free time and rest.
stations.title: Too Busy

stations.challenge: Choose one job: chef, doctor or artist. Say one good thing and one bad thing about it.
followUpQuestions: What jobs seem stressful?
What matters more: money or free time?
What job would you like to try for one day?
stations.mainQuestion: Do you want an interesting job or a well-paid job? Why?
stations.stretch: Invent your dream workplace: people, place and hours. Is less money OK for a job like this? Why?
stations.subtitle: What job do I want?
stations.title: Money or a Job I Love?

stations.challenge: Choose three simple things that make a good life. Compare lists and agree on one.
followUpQuestions: Is a quiet life a good life? Why or why not?
Why do some people want to be famous?
What makes an ordinary day great?
stations.mainQuestion: What do people need to be happy?
stations.stretch: Would you like to be famous one day? Give two reasons for and two reasons against.
stations.subtitle: Do I need to be special?
stations.title: A Normal Life

toolkit.example: Why do you think that? / What about you?

vocabulary.explanation: do what you wanted to do
look at how things are different
time when you do not have to work
money you earn from a job

warmUp.note: If you want: a short activity to start.
warmUp.prompt: Pick three important things in life. Tell your partner one simple reason for each choice.

ui.lessonGoal: Say what you think and give simple reasons.
ui.levelTip: Choose 4 stations. Prepare your question before you speak.

presentation.introduction: School, family, friends, money, the future. What is important to you? Talk about it with a partner.
presentation.privacyNotice: You can invent examples. You don’t need to talk about your grades, your family or your private life.
quickStart: Give a reason or an example.
Need more? Open the next task.
presentation.strap: What is a good life for you?
presentation.subtitle: A conversation, not a test
